title: Strip only a bullet marker plus whitespace from LLM failure-label lines, never a character set
answers: failure label is missing its leading minus sign
symptom starting with -1 or -inf loses the hyphen
evaluation discovery labels drop leading dash characters
why does lstrip eat hyphens from generated symptom text
body:
Symptom: A failure label whose symptom text begins with a hyphen or minus sign loses it, e.g. "-1 returned instead of error" is shown as "1 returned instead of error" and "-inf score emitted" as "inf score emitted".
Root cause: mlflow/genai/discovery/extraction.py:_generate_labels used str.lstrip("- "), which removes every leading '-' and space character, not just one bullet marker.
Fix pattern: Remove the bullet with a compiled prefix regex (_BULLET_PREFIX = r"^\s*[-*+]\s+") that requires whitespace after the marker, then strip the remainder. Keep a regression test with leading-hyphen symptoms in tests/genai/discovery/test_extraction.py:test_extract_failure_labels_keeps_leading_hyphen.
Constraints: Applies to parsing bullet lines of LLM output in extraction.py. Do not reintroduce lstrip/rstrip with a character set for bullet removal. Symptoms that start with a bullet followed directly by a non-space character are treated as content and kept.
applies: Parsing of LLM-generated bullet lists into failure labels in mlflow/genai/discovery/extraction.py; not for other string cleanup.
says: Evaluation failure labels are missing the leading minus sign on negative numbers.
Discovered failure tags drop the initial dash when reporting negative values.
Negative score symptoms in evaluation discovery appear without their starting minus sign.
Generated failure labels should preserve leading hyphens instead of stripping them off.
Failure labels starting with minus one display as positive one on screen.
search: When parsing LLM-generated bullet lists into failure labels in mlflow/genai/discovery/extraction.py:_generate_labels, remove bullet markers using the compiled regex _BULLET_PREFIX requiring whitespace after the marker rather than str.lstrip with a character set. This prevents stripping leading hyphens or minus signs from symptom text such as negative numbers or scores, treating bullets followed immediately by non-space characters as content. Regression coverage is maintained in tests/genai/discovery/test_extraction.py:test_extract_failure_labels_keeps_leading_hyphen, and the rule applies strictly to bullet parsing in extraction.py rather than general string cleanup.
